subject: VAPA
title: Music & Media Arts
description: A year-long arts course that combines music literacy and creation with digital media arts. Semester 1 builds notation, rhythm, harmony, songwriting and critical listening across world and American music traditions, ending in a recorded showcase. Semester 2 applies those skills to media arts: photography and design, audio production and podcasting, video editing and film scoring, culminating in an original multimedia capstone. All production uses free browser tools (BandLab, Chrome Music Lab, Audacity, free video editors).
framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools (Music and Media Arts, High School Proficient)

standards.MU:Cr1.1.HSP: Compose and improvise melodic and rhythmic ideas or motives that reflect characteristic(s) of music from a variety of historical periods.
standards.MU:Cr2.1.HSP: Assemble and organize sounds or short musical ideas to create initial expressions of selected experiences, moods, images, or storylines.
standards.MU:Cr3.1.HSP: Evaluate and refine draft compositions and improvisations based on knowledge, skill, and teacher-provided criteria.
standards.MU:Cr3.2.HSP: Share music through the use of notation, performance, or technology, and demonstrate how the elements of music have been employed.
standards.MU:Pr4.1.HSP: Select music to perform based on interest, knowledge, technical skill, and context.
standards.MU:Pr4.2.HSP: Analyze the structure, context, and performance decisions of selected works and how they inform interpretation, including reading notation.
standards.MU:Pr4.3.HSP: Demonstrate understanding and application of expressive qualities in a varied repertoire.
standards.MU:Pr5.1.HSP: Develop strategies to address technical challenges and evaluate the success of rehearsal strategies.
standards.MU:Pr6.1.HSP: Perform with technical accuracy and expression, demonstrating an understanding of context and audience.
standards.MU:Re7.1.HSP: Explain reasons for selecting music, citing characteristics found in the music and connections to interest, purpose, and context.
standards.MU:Re7.2.HSP: Explain how the analysis of structures and context informs the response to music.
standards.MU:Re8.1.HSP: Explain and support interpretations of the expressive intent and meaning of musical works, citing elements, contexts, and personal research.
standards.MU:Re9.1.HSP: Evaluate works and performances based on personally or collaboratively developed criteria.
standards.MU:Cn10.1.HSP: Demonstrate how interests, knowledge, and skills relate to personal choices and intent when creating, performing, and responding to music.
standards.MU:Cn11.1.HSP: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts, and daily life.
standards.MA:Cr1.1.HSP: Use identified generative methods to formulate multiple ideas, develop artistic goals, and problem solve in media arts creation processes.
standards.MA:Cr2.1.HSP: Apply aesthetic criteria in developing, proposing, and refining artistic ideas, plans, prototypes, and production processes for media arts productions.
standards.MA:Cr3.1.HSP: Consolidate production processes to demonstrate deliberate choices in organizing and integrating content and stylistic conventions to show purpose and meaning.
standards.MA:Pr4.1.HSP: Integrate various arts, media arts forms, and content into unified media arts productions that convey consistent perspectives and narratives.
standards.MA:Pr5.1.HSP: Develop and refine a range of artistic, design, technical, and soft skills through performing various roles in producing media artworks.
standards.MA:Pr6.1.HSP: Design the presentation and distribution of media artworks for intentional impacts through a variety of contexts.
standards.MA:Re7.1.HSP: Analyze and describe the reactions and interpretations of media artworks, considering their intent and context.
standards.MA:Re8.1.HSP: Analyze the intent, meanings, and impacts of diverse media artworks, considering complex factors of context and bias.
standards.MA:Re9.1.HSP: Evaluate media art works and production processes with developed criteria, considering context and artistic goals.
standards.MA:Cn10.1.HSP: Access, evaluate, and integrate personal and external resources to inform the creation of original media artworks.
standards.MA:Cn11.1.HSP: Demonstrate and explain how media artworks and ideas relate to various contexts, purposes, and values, including ethics, copyright and fair use.

units.title: Music Literacy Foundations
units.big_idea: Notation is a code for sound that lets musicians share ideas across time.

units.title: Rhythm, Groove and Beat-Making
units.big_idea: Rhythm organizes time and defines musical styles across cultures.

units.title: Melody, Harmony and Songwriting
units.big_idea: Melodies and chord progressions create emotion and form in songs.

units.title: Listening Across Time and Cultures; Showcase
units.big_idea: Music reflects and shapes the history and values of the people who make it.

units.title: Media Arts Foundations: Image and Design
units.big_idea: Visual composition guides how viewers read meaning in images.

units.title: Audio Production and Podcasting
units.big_idea: Sound design and storytelling create immersive audio experiences.

units.title: Video and Film Scoring
units.big_idea: Picture, sound and music combine to shape a story's emotion.

units.title: Multimedia Capstone
units.big_idea: Artists integrate music and media to communicate a personal vision.

objectives: Read notes on treble and bass clefs

days.title: Musical autobiography
days.work: Write a one-page musical autobiography listing the music that shaped you and set goals for the year.

days.title: Treble clef
days.work: Complete the musictheory.net treble-clef lessons and drill until 90% accuracy.

days.title: Bass clef
days.work: Complete bass-clef lessons and drill; label notes on a printed grand staff.

days.title: Keyboard
days.work: Find all C's, F's and G's on a keyboard app and play a C-major scale with correct fingering.

days.title: Check
days.work: Note-naming quiz (30 notes in 2 minutes).

objectives: Read and count rhythms in simple meter

days.title: Note values
days.work: Learn note and rest values and clap a rhythm ladder.

days.title: Time signatures
days.work: Count and clap rhythms in 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 with a metronome at 80 bpm.

days.title: Dictation
days.work: Notate four 2-measure rhythms you hear (Chrome Music Lab Rhythm).

days.title: Body percussion
days.work: Perform an 8-measure body-percussion piece reading notation.

days.title: Check
days.work: Rhythm reading assessment recorded on video.

days.title: Whole & half steps
days.work: Build major scales using W-W-H-W-W-W-H on a keyboard.

days.title: Key signatures
days.work: Learn the circle of fifths and identify sharp key signatures.

days.title: Flat keys
days.work: Identify flat key signatures.

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Identify and sing intervals using song references (e.g., 'Here Comes the Bride' = P4).

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on scales and intervals.

days.title: Expressive markings
days.work: Learn dynamics, tempo and articulation markings.

days.title: Sight-reading
days.work: Sight-read three 8-bar melodies on keyboard or voice.

days.title: Choose a piece
days.work: Select a short piece (e.g., 'Ode to Joy' or a folk song) to perform.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Use a practice log and slow-practice strategies on difficult measures.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Record a performance and self-evaluate with a rubric.

objectives: Identify rhythmic patterns from world cultures

days.title: Syncopation
days.work: Clap and count syncopated rhythms.

days.title: Clave
days.work: Learn the son clave and play it with salsa recordings.

days.title: West African polyrhythm
days.work: Layer 3-against-2 polyrhythms with family on household drums.

days.title: Listening log
days.work: Listen to rhythms from Brazil, Ghana and India (tala) and note features.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a polyrhythm ensemble.

objectives: Program drum patterns in a DAW

days.title: DAW tour
days.work: Set up a BandLab account and learn the interface.

days.title: Rock beat
days.work: Program a basic rock beat at 100 bpm.

days.title: Hip-hop beat
days.work: Program a hip-hop beat with swing.

days.title: Genre beats
days.work: Program reggaeton dembow and a four-on-the-floor house beat.

days.title: Check
days.work: Share four beats with a labeled screenshot.

objectives: Arrange loops into a song form

days.title: Bass lines
days.work: Write a bass line using root notes of a chord progression.

days.title: Loops
days.work: Explore BandLab loop library and layer three loops.

days.title: Song form
days.work: Analyze form of a favorite song (intro, verse, chorus, bridge).

days.title: Arrange
days.work: Arrange a 90-second instrumental track.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Get feedback from family and revise.

objectives: Create and refine an original instrumental track

days.title: Mixing basics
days.work: Learn volume balance and panning.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Refine your track with automation and fades.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a 150-word artist statement explaining your choices.

days.title: Listening party
days.work: Share your track with family and collect feedback via a criteria sheet.

days.title: Final
days.work: Submit final track.

days.title: Triads
days.work: Build major and minor triads on the keyboard.

days.title: Roman numerals
days.work: Label chords in a key with Roman numerals.

days.title: I-V-vi-IV
days.work: Identify the 'four-chord' progression in five pop songs.

days.title: 12-bar blues
days.work: Play a 12-bar blues progression.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on chords.

objectives: Compose a melody over a progression

days.title: Motifs
days.work: Analyze motifs in Beethoven's Fifth and a pop song.

days.title: Contour
days.work: Sketch melodic contours and turn them into notation.

days.title: Compose
days.work: Compose an 8-bar melody over I-IV-V-I.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for cadence and singability.

days.title: Share
days.work: Share notation and a recording.

days.title: Lyric analysis
days.work: Analyze lyrics of a classic song for hook and rhyme scheme.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Brainstorm themes and write a chorus with a hook.

days.title: Verses
days.work: Write two verses with imagery.

days.title: Prosody
days.work: Match lyric stresses to musical rhythm.

days.title: Check
days.work: Share a lyric draft.

days.title: Set lyrics
days.work: Sing or play your lyric over the chord progression, adjusting the melody so stressed syllables fall on strong beats.

days.title: Bridge
days.work: Write a 4–8 bar bridge that contrasts the chorus by changing chords (e.g., starting on vi or IV) and melodic range.

days.title: Demo
days.work: Record a rough demo in BandLab with a simple guitar/keyboard part and scratch vocal.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Play the demo for a listener and use the 'I like / I wonder / What if' protocol to collect feedback.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise one lyric line, one melodic phrase and the arrangement based on feedback; save as version 2.

objectives: Produce and present an original song

days.title: Record
days.work: Record final vocal or lead instrument tracks, doing at least three takes and choosing the best.

days.title: Mix
days.work: Mix the song: balance levels, pan supporting parts, and add light reverb.

days.title: Lead sheet
days.work: Create a lead sheet in MuseScore or Noteflight with melody, chord symbols and lyrics.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the song to family and explain how melody, harmony and form support the lyric's meaning.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a 250-word reflection on your songwriting process and score yourself on the rubric.

weeks.topic: Western art music: Baroque to Romantic
materials: recordings of Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Chopin (free on YouTube/IMSLP)

days.title: Baroque
days.work: Listen to Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 and identify texture.

days.title: Classical
days.work: Listen to Mozart's Symphony 40 movement 1 and map sonata form.

days.title: Romantic
days.work: Listen to Chopin's Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2 and describe expression.

days.title: Timeline
days.work: Create a timeline connecting periods to world history events.

days.title: Check
days.work: Listening identification quiz.

weeks.topic: American music: spirituals, blues, jazz and rock
objectives: Trace African American roots of popular music

days.title: Spirituals & blues
days.work: Listen to spirituals and Robert Johnson; identify call and response.

days.title: Jazz
days.work: Listen to Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington; describe swing.

days.title: Improvisation
days.work: Improvise over a 12-bar blues using the blues scale.

days.title: Rock & beyond
days.work: Trace rock, soul, hip-hop origins on a family tree.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a 400-word response on how one genre reflects its era.

days.title: Gamelan
days.work: Listen to Balinese gamelan and describe interlocking parts.

days.title: Raga
days.work: Listen to a raga performance and describe its structure.

days.title: Mariachi & son jarocho
days.work: Study mariachi and son jarocho and their role in California.

days.title: Criticism
days.work: Read a professional music review and identify criteria.

days.title: Review
days.work: Write a review of a live or recorded performance.

days.title: Select
days.work: Select pieces for the semester showcase (one performance, one original).

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse with practice log.

days.title: Program notes
days.work: Write program notes.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Hold a dress rehearsal with feedback.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Refine weak passages.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Perform the showcase for family (live or recorded).

days.title: Theory exam
days.work: Take the semester theory exam.

days.title: Listening exam
days.work: Take the listening identification exam.

days.title: Self-evaluation
days.work: Evaluate the showcase recording with a rubric.

days.title: Portfolio
days.work: Organize semester portfolio.

days.title: Media arts intro
days.work: Define media arts and analyze three media works.

days.title: Composition
days.work: Learn rule of thirds, leading lines and framing.

days.title: Photo walk
days.work: Shoot 30 photos applying composition rules.

days.title: Select
days.work: Select the best five and explain choices.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Critique photos with criteria.

days.title: Editing
days.work: Learn exposure, contrast, crop in a free editor.

days.title: Photo essay plan
days.work: Plan a 6-photo essay about your community.

days.title: Shoot
days.work: Shoot the photo essay.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit and sequence images.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the essay with captions.

days.title: Design principles
days.work: Learn CRAP (contrast, repetition, alignment, proximity).

days.title: Typography
days.work: Compare serif, sans-serif and display fonts.

days.title: Album cover
days.work: Design an album cover for your Semester 1 song.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Get feedback and revise.

days.title: Final
days.work: Submit album cover with explanation.

weeks.topic: Copyright, fair use and media ethics

days.title: Copyright
days.work: Learn copyright basics and fair use factors.

days.title: Creative Commons
days.work: Find CC-licensed music and images and attribute them correctly.

days.title: Case studies
days.work: Analyze music sampling lawsuits.

days.title: Media bias
days.work: Analyze how photos are edited to influence viewers.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on copyright and ethics.

days.title: Audacity
days.work: Learn Audacity: record, cut, fade.

days.title: Foley
days.work: Create foley sounds (footsteps, rain) with household objects.

days.title: Soundscape
days.work: Build a 1-minute soundscape of a place.

days.title: Mic technique
days.work: Test mic placement and room acoustics.

days.title: Share
days.work: Share the soundscape.

objectives: Plan and script a podcast episode
materials: Radio Ambulante or NPR podcast examples

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Listen to two podcast episodes (e.g., Radio Ambulante, NPR's Song Exploder) and outline their segments and transitions.

days.title: Topic
days.work: Choose an episode topic (a song's history, a local musician, a genre's California roots) and write a one-sentence pitch.

days.title: Script
days.work: Write a 6–8 minute script with cold open, intro, two segments and outro.

days.title: Interview prep
days.work: Write 8 open-ended interview questions and schedule an interview with a musician or family member.

days.title: Script review
days.work: Read the script aloud with a timer, cutting or adding to hit length.

days.title: Record host
days.work: Record host segments in a quiet, soft-surfaced room, re-recording any flubbed lines.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Record the interview with phone or USB mic, capturing a 30-second room-tone sample.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit the interview down to its best 3 minutes, removing filler and long pauses.

days.title: Music & mix
days.work: Add your original intro music from Unit 2, crossfades between segments, and balanced levels.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Export a draft MP3 and collect feedback from one listener.

days.title: Revise from feedback
days.work: Re-edit the podcast using the three most important notes from the draft feedback, tightening any segment that runs over 2 minutes.

days.title: Show notes & credits
days.work: Write show notes with a 50-word summary, timestamps, and Creative Commons attributions for any music or sound effects used.

days.title: Loudness check
days.work: Normalize the episode in Audacity to a consistent level and export as MP3; compare against a professional podcast's volume.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Score your episode and one professional episode on the same rubric (story, audio quality, pacing, voice) and note gaps.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a 250-word reflection on what you would change for a second episode and why.

days.title: Shot types
days.work: Watch a 3-minute scene from a classic film (e.g., Casablanca airport scene) and log each shot as wide, medium, close-up or extreme close-up.

days.title: Camera angles
days.work: Photograph the same object at high, low, eye-level and Dutch angles and write what feeling each angle creates.

days.title: Editing
days.work: Compare continuity editing in a dialogue scene with Eisenstein's Odessa Steps montage and list how each controls time.

days.title: Storyboard
days.work: Draw a 9-panel storyboard for a 30-second scene with shot type, angle and sound noted under each panel.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz identifying shot types and edits in stills, then revise the storyboard.

objectives: Shoot and edit a short video
materials: free video editor (e.g., DaVinci Resolve or Clipchamp)

days.title: Editor basics
days.work: Import practice clips into a free editor and practice trimming, splitting and ordering clips on the timeline.

days.title: Shoot the scene
days.work: Shoot the storyboarded scene, capturing each shot twice plus 1 minute of B-roll.

days.title: Rough cut
days.work: Assemble a rough cut following the storyboard and note any missing coverage.

days.title: Sound
days.work: Add dialogue clean-up, room tone and one foley effect; adjust audio levels so dialogue is clear.

days.title: Color & export
days.work: Apply basic color correction for consistent shots and export a 1080p file to share.

days.title: Leitmotif
days.work: Listen to themes from Star Wars and Jaws and describe how each leitmotif represents a character or threat.

days.title: Diegetic vs. non-diegetic
days.work: Log every sound in a 2-minute film clip as diegetic or non-diegetic and explain its purpose.

days.title: Two moods
days.work: Score the same 30-second silent clip twice in BandLab—once suspenseful, once comic—changing tempo, key and instrumentation.

days.title: Score your scene
days.work: Compose a 30–60 second underscore for your own scene with a recurring motif.

days.title: Sync & present
days.work: Sync the score to picture so key hits land on cuts, then present both versions and explain choices.

days.title: Concept
days.work: Choose a song (your original or a Creative Commons track) and write a one-paragraph music-video concept: narrative, performance or abstract.

days.title: Storyboard
days.work: Storyboard at least 12 shots mapped to the song's sections (intro, verse, chorus).

days.title: Shoot
days.work: Shoot all footage in one session, including performance and B-roll, with extra takes.

days.title: Edit to the beat
days.work: Edit cuts to land on the beat by marking beats on the timeline; vary pacing between verse and chorus.

days.title: Draft screening
days.work: Screen the draft for one viewer and record three specific suggestions.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Apply the screening suggestions, fixing at least one pacing issue and one visual issue.

days.title: Titles & credits
days.work: Add a title card and end credits with full attribution of music and collaborators.

days.title: Screening night
days.work: Host a family screening of the scored scene and music video and collect written feedback cards.

days.title: Media arts quiz
days.work: Take a quiz on film language, sound design and copyright.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a 300-word comparison of your music video and a professional one using film vocabulary.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Generate three capstone ideas (e.g., a short film with original score, a 3-track EP with album art and lyric videos, an audio documentary) using mind maps.

days.title: Research inspiration
days.work: Collect five reference works (films, albums, podcasts) and note one technique to borrow from each.

days.title: Proposal
days.work: Write a 1-page proposal with artistic goal, audience, tools, and a week-by-week timeline through Week 35.

days.title: Pitch
days.work: Pitch the idea to family in 3 minutes with a mood board and answer questions.

days.title: Pre-production
days.work: Finalize scripts, storyboards or track lists and build a shot/recording checklist.

days.title: Music production
days.work: Compose and record the capstone's music tracks in BandLab, at least 90 seconds of original material.

days.title: Visual production
days.work: Shoot video or create images/graphics for the capstone following the storyboard.

days.title: Audio capture
days.work: Record narration, dialogue or vocals and clean them with noise reduction.

days.title: Rough assembly
days.work: Assemble a complete rough cut or rough mix of the full capstone.

days.title: Timeline check
days.work: Compare progress to the proposal timeline and revise the plan for remaining weeks.

days.title: Critique session
days.work: Show the rough version to two viewers and gather feedback using your proposal's goals as criteria.

days.title: Revise structure
days.work: Re-order, cut or add sections to fix the largest structural issue identified.

days.title: Audio mix
days.work: Balance music, voice and effects; apply EQ to keep dialogue clear and export a test mix.

days.title: Visual polish
days.work: Color-correct, add titles and check every transition and graphic for consistency.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a 300-word artist statement explaining intent, techniques and influences.

days.title: Exhibition prep
days.work: Plan the presentation: format (screening, listening session, web page), order and introduction.

days.title: Exhibit
days.work: Present the capstone to family or a homeschool group with a 2-minute introduction.

days.title: Q&A
days.work: Answer audience questions about your process and choices.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Score the capstone on the rubric (concept, craft, music, media integration, presentation) and compare to audience feedback.

days.title: Final fixes
days.work: Make any final fixes and export archive-quality versions of all files.

days.title: Curate
days.work: Select 6–8 best works from both semesters (performance, song, beat, photo essay, podcast, video, capstone).

days.title: Portfolio site
days.work: Build a free portfolio website or slide portfolio with captions and credits for each work.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the final exam on music theory, history, media arts vocabulary and copyright.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a final reflection on growth as a musician and media artist with evidence from your portfolio.

days.title: Goals
days.work: Set goals for next year's arts course (e.g., Theatre & Performing Arts) and share the portfolio link with family.
